16:10.headline: The "house of turning": a vaulted prison
16:10.body: Asa put the seer in בית המהפכת. Rashi says it was a prison built in that style. Metzudat Zion hears כיפה, "dome", in the word, with its letters turned around, so it was a dome-shaped cell.

sources.quote: בֵּית הַסֹּהַר שֶׁעָשׂוּי מְלֶאכֶת הַמַּהְפֶּכֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it was a prison built with "mahpechet" work.

sources.quote: הוא מל׳ כיפה בהיפוך אותיות והוא מקום מאסר כעין כיפה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from כיפה, "dome", with the letters reversed: a prison shaped like a dome.

16:12.headline: Why Asa's sickness struck his feet
16:12.body: Ralbag sees measure for measure. Asa would not go out to fight Aram and Baasha, though God had helped him before. So God took the strength of his legs. Rashi says the swelling rose from his feet to his head.

sources.quote: הוא לא הסכים ללכת להלחם עם מלך ארם ועם בעשא
sources.says: Ralbag says Asa would not go to fight the king of Aram and Baasha.

sources.quote: ולזה הסיר ה' יתברך מרגליו כח ההליכה
sources.says: Ralbag says that is why God took away the power of walking from his feet.

sources.quote: נֶפַח שֶׁבְּרַגְלָיו עָלָה מִכַּף רַגְלוֹ עַד קָדְקֳדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the swelling in his feet rose from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.

16:12.headline: Asa turned to doctors, not to God
16:12.body: The verse blames Asa for seeking doctors. Ibn Ezra uses it to say doctors may treat outer wounds, but illness inside the body is in God's hand. Malbim says relying on natural means showed his trust was not whole.

sources.quote: לאות שנתן רשות לרופאים לרפא המכות והפצעים שיראו בחוץ רק כל חלי שהוא בפנים בגוף ביד השם לרפאתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says doctors were given permission to heal outer wounds, but illness inside the body is God's to heal.

sources.quote: שסמך עצמו על אמצעיים טבעיים שזה מורה שלא היה בטחונו שלם
sources.says: Malbim says Asa relied on natural means, which shows his trust in God was not complete.

2:5.headline: Who can gather enough strength, or who would hold back?
2:5.body: Rashi reads: who could press together enough strength to build a house fit for God? Ralbag reads: no one should hold back any strength from this building, since even the best is nothing next to God.

sources.quote: מִי יָכוֹל לִדְחוֹק וְלַעֲצוֹר כֹּחַ עַצְמוֹ כָּל כָּךְ לִבְנוֹת לוֹ בַיִת הָרָאוּי לוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it asks who could gather his strength enough to build a house worthy of God.

sources.quote: ומי הוא שימנע כח לבנות לו בית. ר"ל כי אין ראוי לאדם שיבנה לו בית שיעצר מכחו בזה הבנין
sources.says: Ralbag says it asks who would hold back strength, because a person should not hold back any effort in this building.

2:6.headline: Karmil is the scarlet dye, which is otherwise missing here
2:6.body: The Tabernacle's colors were purple, blue and scarlet. Rashi says כרמיל is the scarlet, and proves it: scarlet is not named here any other way.

sources.quote: זוֹ ״תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי״ (שמות כה:ד); תֵּדַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא נִזְכַּר כָּאן תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי
sources.says: Rashi says כרמיל is the scarlet dye, since scarlet is not otherwise mentioned here.

sources.quote: וכרמיל הוא תולעת שני, והוא צבע הכרמז
sources.says: Radak says כרמיל is the scarlet dye, the color called kermes.

2:8.headline: A second 'great house' hints at Solomon's own palace
2:8.body: Solomon already said in verse 4 that the house he builds is great. Malbim says the repeat here hints at his royal palace, and Hiram caught the hint.

sources.quote: וזה מוכרח שכיון בזה על בית מלכותו דהא כבר אמר בפסוק ד' והבית אשר אני בונה גדול, ולמה כפל דבריו
sources.says: Malbim says Solomon must mean his palace here, since he already said in verse 4 that the house is great, so why repeat it?

sources.quote: וחירם באר לו שהבין מה שבלבו שרוצה לבנות גם בית למלכותו
sources.says: Malbim says Hiram showed he understood that Solomon also wanted to build a house for his kingship.

2:12.headline: Huram 'my father': a title, or my father's craftsman?
2:12.body: King Hiram sends 'Huram אבי', literally 'Huram my father'. Rashi reads it as the craftsman who worked for Hiram's father, and Metzudat David adds that אב can be a title of honor, meaning master.

sources.quote: אוּמָּן חָכָם שֶׁל אָבִי הָיָה, גַּם שֶׁלִּי הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says he was my father's skilled craftsman and is mine too.

sources.quote: וקראו אבי בלשון חשיבות על רוב חכמתו כי אב הוא ענין שר וחשוב
sources.says: Metzudat David says Hiram may call him 'my father' as an honor for his great skill, since אב can mean a master.

2:13.headline: Rachel's sons Dan and Naphtali share in building God's house
2:13.body: Rashi says his mother was from Dan and his father from Naphtali. He reads Rachel's naming of Naphtali, 'my twistings', as her claim to match Leah: when Leah's descendants build God's house, sons of Dan and Naphtali build with them.

sources.quote: ״נַפְתּוּלֵי אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹ׳״ (בראשית ל:ח) – אָמְרָה רָחֵל: מֵעַתָּה עִקַּמְתִּי פְּתוּלִים
sources.says: Rashi says that when Rachel named Naphtali she said she had made twists to match her sister.

sources.quote: אִם לֵאָה תִּתְפָּאֵר בִּבְצַלְאֵל בְּנָהּ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הַמִּשְׁכָּן, יִצְטָרֵךְ לְהִשְׁתַּתֵּף בִּמְלַאכְתּוֹ אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי דָן
sources.says: Rashi says if Leah's descendant Betzalel made the Tabernacle, a son of Dan had to share the work, and so with Solomon's Temple.

2:16.headline: An extra letter marks when the strangers were put to work
2:16.body: Here הגירים is spelled with two yods, but when David counted them it had one. Rashi says the full spelling marks the time of the actual work, when Solomon built.

sources.quote: מָלֵא בִּשְׁנֵי יוֹדִי״ן
sources.says: Rashi notes the word is spelled full, with two yods.

sources.quote: אֲבָל שְׁלֹמֹה סְפָרָם בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה כְּשֶׁבָּנָה, וּלְכָךְ כְּתִיב מָלֵא
sources.says: Rashi says Solomon counted them at the time of the work, when he built, so it is spelled full.

24:4.headline: To renew the Temple meant more than patching it up
24:4.body: לחדש means to make new. Malbim stops on the word: Joash wanted to bring the Temple back to its beauty on the day it was built, not only to fix what was broken.

sources.quote: שיואש רצה לחדש את בית ה', היינו להעמידו ביופיו כמו שהיה בעת הבנין
sources.says: Malbim says Joash wanted to renew the Temple, meaning to set it up in its beauty as it was when first built.

sources.quote: לחדש. לתקנו ולבנות מה מחדש
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means to repair it and rebuild parts of it anew.

24:6.headline: The Temple tax is named after the Torah's words כי תשא
24:6.body: משאת means something brought as a gift. Rashi and Radak say this tax of Moses takes its name from כי תשא, when you count the people, the Torah verse that set the yearly half-shekel.

sources.quote: משאת. על שם ״כי תשא״
sources.says: Rashi says the word משאת is named after the phrase כי תשא.

sources.quote: ומפני זה קראו "משאת", על שם "כי תשא"
sources.says: Radak says this is the half-shekel all Israel gave once a year, and it is called משאת after the Torah's words כי תשא.

sources.quote: משאת. ענין דורון ותשורה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says משאת means a present or gift.

24:7.headline: Athaliah's sons: the commentators say they were not the king's
24:7.body: The verse blames Athaliah's sons for breaking into the Temple. Radak and Metzudat David stop to say these were sons she had by another man, not by the king.

sources.quote: ופי' "בניה": בנים שהיו לה מאיש אחר, ולא מן המלך
sources.says: Radak says her sons means sons she had from another man, not from the king.

sources.quote: בניה. שהיו לה מאיש אחר
sources.says: Metzudat David says these were sons she had from another man.

24:7.headline: "All" the holy things here means most of them
24:7.body: The verse says Athaliah's family gave all the Temple's holy things to the Baals. Radak says כל here means most, because the book of Kings shows some treasures were still there later.

sources.quote: לפיכך אמ' "כל", שפרושו כמו "רב", כמו "וכל טוב אדניו בידו"
sources.says: Radak says כל here means most, as in the verse about all his master's goods in his hand.

sources.quote: והראיה כי נשארו מן הקדשים בבית יי' מה שאומר בספר מלכים
sources.says: Radak says the proof that some holy things were left is what the book of Kings tells later.

24:13.headline: The repairs are described as healing the Temple
24:13.body: ארוכה means healing, like a wound closing. Metzudat Zion says it is borrowed here for strengthening a building, and Radak compares Elijah, who healed the broken altar.

sources.quote: הוא ענין רפואה ובא בדרך השאלה על חיזוק הבנין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means healing and is borrowed for strengthening the building.

sources.quote: בדרך ההשאלה. וכן "כי עלתה ארוכה לחומת ירושלם" (נח' ד,א); וכן "וירפא את מזבח יי' ההרוס"
sources.says: Radak says this is borrowed speech, like the healing of Jerusalem's wall in Nehemiah and the healing of the broken altar.

sources.quote: ותעל ארוכה למלאכה. דגמא: ״היחיו האבנים״
sources.says: Rashi compares the phrase will they bring the stones back to life, said about rebuilding in Nehemiah.

24:17.headline: The officials bowed to Joash as if he were a god
24:17.body: Bowing to a king is normal. But the sages, quoted by Radak and Malbim, say these officials bowed to Joash as a god, because he had hidden in the Temple for six years and lived.

sources.quote: ובדרש: "וישתחוו" לו – שעשאוהו אלוה
sources.says: Radak brings a midrash that they bowed to him because they made him a god.

sources.quote: ואתה היית בבית המקדש שש שנים
sources.says: Radak says they told him he had been in the Temple six years and was still alive.

sources.quote: שהשתחוו לו לשם אלהות
sources.says: Malbim says the sages explained that they bowed to him as to a god.

24:20.headline: Zechariah stood above the people: on high ground, or in rank?
24:20.body: Rashi first reads מעל לעם simply: he stood higher than the crowd so all could hear. He also brings a midrash that Zechariah trusted in being above the people, as a prophet, a priest and the king's son-in-law, and so was not afraid to speak.

sources.quote: גבוה מכל העם כדי להשמיע קולו
sources.says: Rashi says he stood higher than all the people so his voice would be heard.

sources.quote: סמך על עצמו שהיה שר גבוה מכל העם, נביא וכהן
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that he relied on being a great man above all the people, a prophet and a priest.

24:23.headline: Punishment came as the sun circled back to the murder's date
24:23.body: תקופה means a turning or circuit. Metzudat David says the army came just as the sun returned to where it stood when Zechariah was killed, one full year later.

sources.quote: כאשר הקיפה החמה לבא אל הנקודה ההיא בעצמה שעמדה בעת שנהרג
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means when the sun went around and came back to the same point where it stood when he was killed.

sources.quote: וכן היה, כי מיד נדרש דמו, כי לתקופת השנה
sources.says: Rashi says Zechariah's blood was avenged right away, at the turn of the year.

24:24.headline: "Judgments" on Joash meant harsh suffering
24:24.body: שפטים usually means judgments. Metzudat David and Malbim read it as harsh suffering done to Joash, and Malbim says the sages saw a shameful abuse in it, a punishment for letting himself be made a god.

sources.quote: עשו שפטים. עשו בו דין משפט יסורין
sources.says: Metzudat David says they carried out on him a judgment of suffering.

sources.quote: ענוים קשים, וחז"ל פירשו שענוהו
sources.says: Malbim says it means harsh torments, and that the sages explained they abused him.

sources.quote: וזה עונש על שעשה א"ע אלוה
sources.says: Malbim says this was a punishment for making himself a god.

24:25.headline: "The blood of the sons", though only one son was killed
24:25.body: Only Zechariah was killed, yet the verse says the sons of Jehoiada. Radak and Metzudat David say the Bible can use the plural for one, as in ובני דן חושים, the sons of Dan: Hushim; Ralbag says it counts the children Zechariah would have had.

sources.quote: ואמ' "בדמי בני יהוידע" כמו "ובני דן חושים"
sources.says: Radak says the sons of Jehoiada can mean one son, like the sons of Dan: Hushim.

sources.quote: ועם שרק זכריהו נהרג אמר בני וכן ובני דן חושים
sources.says: Metzudat David says that though only Zechariah was killed, the verse says sons, as with the sons of Dan.

sources.quote: והנה אמר דמי בני יהוידע הכהן בעבור הבנים שעתידים לצאת ממנו
sources.says: Ralbag says the verse speaks of sons because of the children who would have come from him.

24:26.headline: Why the killers' Moabite and Ammonite mothers are named
24:26.body: Rashi asks why the verse names the plotters' mothers as an Ammonite and a Moabite. Citing the Mekhilta, he says these nations forgot Abraham's kindness to their father Lot, so they were fit to punish Joash, who forgot Jehoiada's kindness.

sources.quote: אלא יבאו כפויי טובה, שכפו טובתו של אברהם אבינו ללוט אביהם
sources.says: Rashi says ungrateful people should come, those who denied Abraham's kindness to their father Lot.

sources.quote: ויפרעו מיואש שכפה טובתו של יהוידע והרג את זכריה בנו
sources.says: Rashi says they punished Joash, who denied Jehoiada's kindness and killed his son Zechariah.

24:27.headline: A burden of prophecy, or the name of Joash's son?
24:27.body: משא means a burden, and also a prophecy spoken against someone. Metzudat David reads it as the many prophecies against Joash; Malbim, following the word as it is read aloud, says ירב המשא עליו was the name of one of his sons.

sources.quote: מרבית הנבואות שנבאו עליו הנביאים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the many prophecies the prophets spoke against him.

sources.quote: ולפי הקרי, כן היה שם בניו, א' נקרא בשם ירב המשא עליו
sources.says: Malbim says that by the way the word is read, these were his sons' names, and one was called ירב המשא עליו.

24:27.headline: The "Midrash" of the Book of Kings was a record of events
24:27.body: In the Bible מדרש appears only twice. Metzudat David says the chronicle of the kings is called מדרש because the kings' stories are looked into there; Ralbag thinks it was a book we no longer have.

sources.quote: הספר של דברי הימים מהמלכים נקרא מדרש כי בו נדרש ספורי עניני המלכים והקורות
sources.says: Metzudat David says the chronicle of the kings is called מדרש because the stories of the kings and events are looked into in it.

sources.quote: או הוא ספר אחר בלתי נמצא אצלנו והוא היותר נכון
sources.says: Ralbag says it may be another book that we do not have, and he thinks this is more likely.

26:5.headline: Who is Zechariah: the king himself, or a prophet?
26:5.body: Rashi says Zechariah is another name for Uzziah, a king called by three names: Uzziah, Zechariah and Azariah. Radak says this Zechariah was a prophet.

sources.quote: זֶה עֻזִּיָּהוּ, וּשְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת נִקְרְאוּ לוֹ: עֻזִּיָּהוּ, זְכַרְיָהוּ, עֲזַרְיָהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says Zechariah is Uzziah, who had three names: Uzziah, Zechariah and Azariah.

sources.quote: בימי זכריה המבין בראת האלהים. פי': שהיה נביא
sources.says: Radak says the verse means this Zechariah was a prophet.

26:8.headline: The 'Ammonites' here may be the Meunites, letters swapped
26:8.body: Verse 7 names the Meunites, and verse 8 says the Ammonites brought tribute. Radak says these are the same Meunites with the letters reversed, and Metzudat David says perhaps so.

sources.quote: הם המעונים שזכר (לעיל פס' ז), והוא הפוך
sources.says: Radak says they are the Meunites mentioned before, with the name reversed.

sources.quote: אולי הם המעונים שזכר והוא הפוך
sources.says: Metzudat David says perhaps they are the Meunites, with the name reversed.

sources.quote: והמעונים. ידמה שהם העמונים
sources.says: Ralbag, going the other way, says the Meunites seem to be the Ammonites.

26:10.headline: Loving the soil: the midrash pairs Uzziah with Cain
26:10.body: The verse says Uzziah loved the soil. Rashi cites Bereshit Rabbah: two men chased after the soil and no good came of them, Uzziah and Cain, while Malbim reads it as praise: he farmed so the land would have bread.

sources.quote: שְׁנַיִם לְהוּטִים אַחֲרֵי אֲדָמָה הָיוּ, וְלֹא נִמְצָא בָם תּוֹעֶלֶת, הוּא וְקַיִן
sources.says: Rashi cites the midrash that two men were eager for the soil and no good came of them: Uzziah and Cain.

sources.quote: והיה עוסק בעבודת אדמה שיהיה בר ומזון בא"י ולא ישאו חרפת רעב
sources.says: Malbim says he worked the land so Israel would have grain and food and not suffer the shame of hunger.

26:15.headline: Clever war machines, named for careful thinking
26:15.body: חשבנות comes from חשב, to think or plan. Rashi links it to the skilled work of the Tabernacle and says these were war machines like battering rams, and Malbim says Uzziah knew mechanics and built machines to hurl stones from the walls.

sources.quote: דֻּגְמָא ״מַעֲשֵׂה חוֹשֵׁב״ (שמות כו:א), כְּלֵי מִלְחָמוֹת עָשָׂה בְאוּמָנוּת, כְּגוֹן דִּיק וְאֵילִים הַמְנַגְּחִים בַּחוֹמָה
sources.says: Rashi compares it to the skilled work of the Tabernacle and says he made war machines, like siege towers and rams that strike the wall.

sources.quote: היה חכם גדול בחכמת החשבון והמעכאניק שע"י מלאכת מחשבת יניעו משאות כבדות
sources.says: Malbim says he was expert in calculation and mechanics, making machines that move heavy loads.

26:16.headline: A high heart can be good, but his went too far
26:16.body: גבה לבו, 'his heart grew high', can be praise, as when Jehoshaphat's heart was high in God's ways. Malbim says Uzziah's went past the right measure, until he thought he deserved the high priesthood.

sources.quote: כי לפעמים יהיה גבהות הלב לטובה כמ"ש ביהושפט ויגבה לבו בדרכי ה', אבל הוא גבה לבו יותר מן המדה עד להשחית, שחשב בגבהו שהוא ראוי לכהונה גדולה
sources.says: Malbim says a high heart is sometimes good, as with Jehoshaphat, but Uzziah's grew too high, so he thought himself fit for the high priesthood.

26:16.headline: Was Uzziah's trespass a mistake or a grab for power?
26:16.body: Rashi says the word מעל fits because Uzziah acted by mistake, as in Leviticus 5:15. Malbim says he wanted religion under his control too, so he reached for the priesthood.

sources.quote: כָּאן נוֹפֵל לוֹמַר מְעִילָה, כִּי בִּשְׁגָגָה עָשָׂה
sources.says: Rashi says the word for trespass fits here because he did it by mistake.

sources.quote: וע"כ רצה בכהונה שיהיה גם הדת תחת רשותו
sources.says: Malbim says he wanted the priesthood so that religion would also be under his rule.

26:19.headline: Leprosy that 'shone' on his forehead
26:19.body: זרחה usually describes the sun rising and shining. Metzudat David says it is used here because the leprosy was white and gleamed, and Malbim says it broke out on his forehead as a sign of his bad thoughts.

sources.quote: לזה אמר לשון זריחה כי מבהיק בעבור הלובן
sources.says: Metzudat David says the verse uses the word for shining because the white leprosy gleamed.

sources.quote: ובתוך זעפו זרחה הצרעת במצחו לסימן על רוע מחשבותיו
sources.says: Malbim says the leprosy broke out on his forehead as a sign of his bad thoughts.

26:21.headline: A 'house of freedom': free of ruling, or among the dead
26:21.body: Metzudat David says the king became free of the work of ruling. Rashi and Radak cite the Jerusalem Talmud: he lived in a house in the cemetery, from 'free among the dead' in Psalms 88:6.

sources.quote: עזב הנהגת המלוכה והיה חפשי מן העמל
sources.says: Metzudat David says he left the running of the kingdom and was free of its labor.

sources.quote: עָשָׂה לוֹ בַּיִת בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת; עַל שֵׁם ״בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי״
sources.says: Rashi cites the Jerusalem Talmud that he made himself a house in the cemetery, after 'free among the dead'.

sources.quote: מפרש בתלמוד ירושלמי שעשה לו בית בבית הקברות
sources.says: Radak says the Jerusalem Talmud explains he made himself a house in the cemetery.

3:1.headline: Mount Moriah: where God was seen, where Isaac was bound
3:1.body: The verse ties the place to seeing: on Moriah God appeared to David. Ralbag learns from this that the Temple stood where Isaac was bound, and Malbim links it to Abraham's words there, on the LORD's mountain he will be seen.

sources.quote: לְפִי אֲשֶׁר שָׁם נִרְאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדָוִד בְּגֹרֶן אָרְנָן
sources.says: Rashi says it is because God appeared there to David at Araunah's threshing floor.

sources.quote: למדנו מזה כי במקו' שנעקד יצחק שם היה
sources.says: Ralbag says we learn that the Temple stood on the spot where Isaac was bound.

sources.quote: בהר ה' יראה, ששם יראה ה' בעתיד ותתגלה שכינתו
sources.says: Malbim links it to on the LORD's mountain he will be seen, the place where God's presence would later appear.

3:3.headline: Founded, or counseled? A plan as a building's foundation
3:3.body: Ralbag reads הוסד as the laying of foundations. Radak reads it as taking counsel, since a plan is the foundation of any work, and he says Solomon's plan came from David.

sources.quote: הנה הוסד הוא מקור והרצון בו ההתיסד שעשה שלמה
sources.says: Ralbag says הוסד refers to the founding that Solomon did.

sources.quote: והכל ענין יסוד, כי העצה והסוד למעשה כיסוד לבנין
sources.says: Radak says it means taking counsel, because counsel is to an action what a foundation is to a building.

sources.quote: והעצה והסוד בבנין הבית לקח שלמה מדוד אביו
sources.says: Radak says Solomon took the plan for the house from his father David.

3:3.headline: The first measure: the Tabernacle's cubit, or David's survey?
3:3.body: Radak and Metzudat David say it means the cubit used for the Tabernacle, six handbreadths long. Malbim adds another reading: David had measured when he dug the foundations, and Solomon kept his father's first measure.

sources.quote: במדה שנעשה בה המשכן וכליו – כאותה האמה היא האמה הזאת
sources.says: Radak says it is the same cubit with which the Tabernacle and its vessels were made.

sources.quote: במדת האמה שנעשה בה המשכן שהיתה ראשונה לבנין המקדש והיא היתה בת ששה טפחים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the Tabernacle's cubit, six handbreadths long.

sources.quote: ומשמיענו ששלמה לא שינה המדה הראשונה שמדד אביו
sources.says: Malbim says it may teach that Solomon did not change the first measurements his father made.

3:4.headline: A hall 120 cubits tall, when Kings says thirty?
3:4.body: Kings gives the house a height of thirty cubits, but here the height is 120. Rashi says thirty reached the first upper floor and the upper stories added ninety more, while Radak thinks the front hall alone rose that high, with upper rooms inside it.

sources.quote: גֹּבַהּ הַקּוֹמָה מִקַּרְקָעִית הַבַּיִת עַד קֵרוּי עֲלִיָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה שְׁלֹשִׁים אַמּוֹת, וּמֵעֲלִיָּה לַעֲלִיָּה עַד גַּג הָעֶלְיוֹן תִּשְׁעִים אַמּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it was thirty cubits to the first upper floor and ninety more up to the top roof.

sources.quote: והקרוב אצלי כי האולם לבדו היה לו זה הגבה, ובו היו העליות
sources.says: Radak thinks only the front hall had this height, and the upper rooms were in it.

3:6.headline: Parvaim gold: a place, or gold red as bulls' blood?
3:6.body: Rashi and Radak say Parvaim is a place name. They also bring the Sages, who heard פרים, bulls, in the name: the gold was so fine and red that it looked like bulls' blood.

sources.quote: פַּרְוָיִם, שֵׁם מָקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says Parvaim is the name of a place.

sources.quote: שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לְדַם פָּרִים מֵרוֹב שִׁבְחוֹ וְאַדְמִימוּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi brings the Sages, who say it looked like bulls' blood because of its quality and redness.

sources.quote: שהיה אדום כדם הפרים
sources.says: Radak brings the Sages' view that it was red like the blood of bulls.

3:10.headline: A one-time word: childlike figures, or wings in motion?
3:10.body: צעצעים appears only here. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it like צאצאים, offspring, so the cherubim had the shape of children, while Ralbag reads it as spreading and Malbim as wings made to look as if in flight.

sources.quote: תַּבְנִית יְלָדִים וִילָדוֹת עָשָׂה לַכְּרוּבִים
sources.says: Rashi says he made the cherubim in the form of boys and girls.

sources.quote: צעצעים. כמו צאצאים באל״ף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says צעצעים is like צאצאים, offspring.

sources.quote: ונראה לי שהרצון בו מעשה פרישות
sources.says: Ralbag says in his view it means work that spreads out, the cherubim spreading their wings.

sources.quote: נראה פירושו שהיו נראים כפורחים
sources.says: Malbim says it means they looked as if they were flying.

3:13.headline: Moses' cherubim faced each other; Solomon's faced the room
3:13.body: In the Torah the cherubim face each other, but Solomon's face the house. Radak says these were simply made differently, and brings the Sages, who say their faces turned partly aside, like a student taking leave of his teacher.

sources.quote: יתכן לפרש כי נשתנו בזה, כמו שנשתנו שהיו עומדים על רגליהם
sources.says: Radak says these cherubim may simply have differed in this, as they differed in standing on their feet.

sources.quote: ואמרו שהיו מצדדין את פניהם כתלמיד הנפטר מרבו
sources.says: Radak brings the Sages, who say their faces were turned aside like a student leaving his teacher.

sources.quote: וכרובים שהוסיף שלמה באו לרמז שגם בעת שלא יעשו רצונו של מקום
sources.says: Malbim says Solomon's added cherubim hint at times when Israel does not do God's will.

3:14.headline: A curtain where there were already doors
3:14.body: The inner room had doors, yet Solomon also hung a curtain. Radak says the doors were left open so the Ark's poles could be seen, and Malbim notes the curtain is not mentioned in Kings.

sources.quote: לפי שלא היו נסגרות כדי שיראו הבדים על פני הדביר
sources.says: Radak says the doors were not closed, so the poles could be seen in front of the inner room.

sources.quote: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ דְּלָתוֹת תָּלָה עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says he hung the curtain even though the doorway had doors.

sources.quote: זה לא נזכר במלכים והוסיפו עזרא
sources.says: Malbim says the curtain is not mentioned in Kings, and Ezra added it.

3:15.headline: A one-time word for the pillar's cap: a covering, or a lookout
3:15.body: צפת appears only here, for the cap that Kings calls a כותרת, a crown. Rashi reads it as a covering over the pillar, and Malbim adds that it may come from צניף, a turban, or from צופה, one who watches from above.

sources.quote: צֶפֶת הוּא צִפּוּי כְּמוֹ וַיְצַפֶּה אוֹתָם זָהָב
sources.says: Rashi says צפת means a covering, as in he covered them with gold.

sources.quote: מלשון צניף, או על שעומד כצופה מלמעלה
sources.says: Malbim says it comes from the word for a turban, or from standing like a lookout on top.

sources.quote: וקרוהי צפת לפי שהיתה צפוי וכסוי על העמוד ממעל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is called צפת because it was a covering on top of the pillar.

3:16.headline: Chains in the inner room, or on the pillars outside?
3:16.body: דביר is the Temple's inner room, but the pillars stood outside at the entrance. Radak says the verse speaks of two sets of chains, while Ralbag and Malbim say דביר here names the inner, covered part of the pillar's cap.

sources.quote: אינו אומר שאותן שרשרות שבדביר נתן על ראש העמודים, שהרי העמודים היו באולם על פני ההיכל
sources.says: Radak says the chains in the inner room were not the ones put on the pillars, since the pillars stood in the front hall.

sources.quote: כן קרא דביר שם הכותרת הפנימית
sources.says: Ralbag says the inner part of the capital is called דביר, like the inner room.

sources.quote: וקרא תחתית השבכה בשם דביר, שהוא החדר הפנימי המכוסה
sources.says: Malbim says the lower part of the netting is called דביר, after the covered inner room.

3:17.headline: Yachin: may the house stand firm
3:17.body: Radak and Metzudat David read יכין as a good sign that the house will stand firm forever. Rashi ties it to David's kingdom, established forever like the moon, or to Samson, an ancestor of the craftsman Hiram, who grasped two pillars.

sources.quote: לשון הכנה, כלומ' שיכון הבית לעולם
sources.says: Radak says יכין means being established, that the house will stand forever.

sources.quote: יכין. לסימן טוב שיכין הבית לעד
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a good sign that the house will stand forever.

sources.quote: יָכִין עַל שֵׁם מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל לְיָרֵחַ
sources.says: Rashi says Yachin is named for David's kingdom, which is compared to the moon.

sources.quote: חִירָם שֶׁהָיָה מִבְּנֵי דָן עָשָׂה אֶת הָעַמּוּדִים, קָרָא אֶת הָאֶחָד יָכִין עַל שֵׁם אָבִיו שִׁמְשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi also says Hiram, from the tribe of Dan, named one pillar Yachin after his ancestor Samson.

32:1.headline: Why does Sennacherib attack right after Hezekiah's "faithful deeds"?
32:1.body: The verse says Sennacherib came "after these deeds of faithfulness". Radak says the king was faithful but the people were not. Malbim says it was no punishment: God brought Sennacherib so a miracle could happen for Hezekiah.

sources.quote: כי אע"פ שחזקיהו היה לבו שלם, ביהודה היו דברים רעים
sources.says: Radak says that although Hezekiah's heart was whole, there were evil things in Judah.

sources.quote: בא להוציא בל נאמר שבא סנחריב עליו ע"י איזה חטא שרצה ה' להענישו
sources.says: Malbim says the verse comes to rule out that Sennacherib came because of a sin God wanted to punish.

sources.quote: רק זה היה בהשגחה שיעשה נס על ידו
sources.says: Malbim says it was God's plan, so that a miracle would be done through him.

32:5.headline: שלח: a weapon, not a "sending"
32:5.body: שלח usually means "send". Here it is a weapon. Rashi and Radak say it means a sword, or weapons in general. Malbim says it is a special blade, part sword and part spear.

sources.quote: שלח לרב. חרב, והוא כלל לכל כלי זיין
sources.says: Radak says it means a sword, and stands for all weapons.

sources.quote: כְּלֵי זַיִן, דֻּגְמַת ״וְאִישׁ שִׁלְחוֹ בְּיָדוֹ״
sources.says: Rashi says it means weapons, as in "each man with his שלח in his hand".

sources.quote: ששלח מובדל מן חרב שהוא החרב החדה בראשה הדוקרת ועשויה בתבנית חרב ורומח יחד
sources.says: Malbim says a שלח differs from a sword: it is sharp at the tip for stabbing, made like a sword and spear in one.

32:5.headline: The Millo, "the filling", a square where people gathered
32:5.body: Metzudat Zion and Ralbag say the Millo was an open space outside the wall of the City of David. It was called this because people gathered and filled it, as in "they called a full crowd after you".

sources.quote: מקום מוכן לאסיפת העם כמו קראו אחריך מלא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it was a place set aside for the people to gather, as in Jeremiah 12.

sources.quote: וחוץ מן החומה היה רחוב שהיו מתקבצים בו ולזה נקרא מלוא
sources.says: Ralbag says outside the wall was a square where people gathered, and so it was called Millo.

32:7.headline: חִזְקוּ: be strong yourselves, not "strengthen others"
32:7.body: Rashi notes a difference in the vowels. חַזְּקוּ means "strengthen others". Here the vowels read חִזְקוּ, which means "be strong yourselves", as Hezekiah tells his people.

sources.quote: וְאִם הָיָה בָּא לוֹמַר חִזְקוּ אַתֶּם שֶׁיֶּדְכֶם רָפוֹת, הָיָה לִנָּקֵד ״חִזְקוּ וְאִמְצוּ״
sources.says: Rashi says that to tell people to be strong themselves, the word would be voweled חִזְקוּ, as in this verse.

32:12.headline: Sennacherib mocks "one altar": how can one serve so many?
32:12.body: Sennacherib's envoy says Hezekiah removed God's altars and left one. Rashi says he argued: what use is one altar for so great a people? They thought the high places Hezekiah removed were built for Israel's God.

sources.quote: וּמַה מּוֹעִיל אֶחָד לְעַם רַב כָּזֶה
sources.says: Rashi says the envoy asked what use one altar is for so large a people.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ סְבוּרִים, שֶׁכָּל אוֹתָן בָּמוֹת שֶׁהֵסִיר
sources.says: Rashi says they thought all the high places he removed had been built for the God of Israel.

32:21.headline: Which angel struck the camp? The Targum names two
32:21.body: The verse says God sent "an angel". The Targum names Michael and Gabriel. It says they struck on Passover night with fire that burned the soldiers' souls inside their bodies.

sources.quote: וּשְׁדַר מֵימְרָא דַייָ מִיכָאֵל וְגַבְרִיאֵל מַלְאָכָא וְשֵׁיצֵי בְּלֵילְוָא דְפִסְחָא
sources.says: The Targum says the Lord sent the angels Michael and Gabriel, who destroyed them on the night of Passover.

sources.quote: וְאוֹקִיד נִשְׁמַתְהוֹן בִּגְוַתְהוֹן
sources.says: The Targum says it burned their souls within their bodies.

32:22.headline: God "led them gently", as a shepherd leads by still waters
32:22.body: נהל means to lead slowly and gently. Metzudat Zion compares Psalm 23, "He leads me by still waters". Malbim says the word is used for leading one who has no strength of his own.

sources.quote: ענין הנהגה בנחת כמו על מי מנוחות ינהלני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means gentle leading, as in "by still waters He leads me".

sources.quote: מורה על הנהגה בנחת, את מי שאין לו כח בעצמו
sources.says: Malbim says it means gentle leading of one who has no strength himself.

32:24.headline: A "sign" or a "wonder"? Malbim says the sun truly stopped
32:24.body: Kings calls the sign of Hezekiah's healing an אות, "a sign". Here it is a מופת, "a wonder". Malbim says the word was chosen to teach that the sun itself stood still. Some, like Ralbag, said only the shadow moved.

sources.quote: שגדר המופת הוא דבר זר היוצא מן הטבע, כי השמש בעצמו עמדה אז
sources.says: Malbim says a מופת is something strange, outside nature, because the sun itself stood still then.

sources.quote: והתפלספו קצת לאמר שרק הצל נטה לא השמש כמ"ש הרלב"ג
sources.says: Malbim says some reasoned that only the shadow moved, not the sun, as Ralbag wrote.

32:25.headline: How did Hezekiah's heart grow proud?
32:25.body: Rashi says Hezekiah showed his whole treasure house to the envoys from Babylon. Malbim also suggests his storing up gold and silver, which the Torah forbids a king "so that his heart not be lifted up".

sources.quote: שֶׁהֶרְאָה ״אֶת כָּל בֵּית נְכֹתוֹ וְגוֹ׳״
sources.says: Rashi says he showed the envoys his whole treasure house.

sources.quote: שעשה לו אוצרות לזהב ולכסף, שזה אסור למלך
sources.says: Malbim says he made himself treasuries of gold and silver, which is forbidden to a king.

32:31.headline: מליצי: envoys, literally "interpreters"
32:31.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say a messenger is called מליץ, as Joseph spoke to his brothers through a מליץ, an interpreter. The messenger carries words between sender and receiver. The Targum also says "interpreters".

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהַשָּׁלִיחַ מֵלִיץ בֵּין הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ לַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says a messenger is so called because he interprets between the sender and the one he is sent to.

sources.quote: השליח נקרא מליץ כי מביא דברי המשלח אל מי שנשלח אליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a messenger is called מליץ because he brings the sender's words to the receiver.

sources.quote: בִּמְתוּרְגְמָנֵי רַבָּנֵי מַלְכָּא דְבָבֶל
sources.says: The Targum calls them the interpreters of the king of Babylon's officers.

32:33.headline: Buried on "the ascent", or in the place of honor?
32:33.body: The Targum reads במעלה as "on the ascent" of the royal tombs. Rashi and Radak, after the Talmud, read it as the best place: beside the greatest of the family, David and Solomon.

sources.quote: בְּמַסוֹקְיַת קִבְרֵי בְּנֵי דָוִד
sources.says: The Targum renders it "on the ascent of the graves of David's sons".

sources.quote: במקום המעֻלה שבהם, כלומ': עם הטובים שבהם
sources.says: Radak says it means in the best place among them, with the best of them.

sources.quote: ומאן נינהו? דוד ושלמה
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages: who are these? David and Solomon.

34:9.headline: Guards of the doorway, or of the holy vessels?
34:9.body: סף can mean a doorway. Metzudat Zion reads the phrase as gatekeepers. Ralbag says these Levites guarded the holy vessels and holy things.

sources.quote: והם השוערים כי סף היא ענין מזוזה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they were the gatekeepers, since סף means a doorpost.

sources.quote: הם הממונים על שמירת כלי הקודש והקדשים
sources.says: Ralbag says they were the men in charge of guarding the holy vessels and holy things.

34:10.headline: To check the building, or to fix its cracks?
34:10.body: Today בדק means to check. Metzudat Zion says here it means fixing the בדק, the broken spot, so called because people search for it. Malbim reads it in order: first inspect the house, then repair what they find.

sources.quote: לתקן הבדק והוא מקום השבור וההרוס ונקרא בדק ע״ש שבודקין ומחפשין אחריו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means repairing the breach, which is called בדק because people search for it.

sources.quote: פירוש אחר שיבדקו הבית, ואם ימצאו שם קלקול יחזקוהו
sources.says: Malbim says they first inspected the house and then strengthened whatever was damaged.

34:14.headline: "By the hand of Moses": written in his own hand
34:14.body: ביד משה usually means through Moses. Malbim and Metzudat David read it literally: the scroll Moses himself wrote. Rashi says the book was Deuteronomy.

sources.quote: שמצא את הספר תורה שכתבו משה בעצמו
sources.says: Malbim says Hilkiah found the Torah scroll that Moses wrote himself.

sources.quote: ביד משה. ר״ל מה שכתב משה בידו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means what Moses wrote with his hand.

sources.quote: מִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the book was Deuteronomy.

34:22.headline: Huldah lived in the "second" quarter, or in a house of study
34:22.body: משנה means second. Rashi says she lived between the city's two walls. The Aramaic translation and Radak read it as a house of Torah study, from the sense of learning.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵי חוֹמוֹת הָיוּ לָעִיר, וְהִיא יוֹשֶׁבֶת בֵּין שְׁנֵי הַחוֹמוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the city had two walls and she lived between them.

sources.quote: וְתַרְגּוּמוֹ: ״בֵּית אוּלְפָנָא״
sources.says: Rashi adds that the Aramaic translation renders it 'house of learning'.

sources.quote: במשנה. בבית המדרש
sources.says: Radak says it means in the house of study, as משנה can mean learning Torah.

35:13.headline: "They boiled" the Passover lamb, though it had to be roasted
35:13.body: The Passover lamb must be roasted, not boiled in water. Radak says this is the only place the word for cooking means roasting, so the verse adds "in fire". Ralbag learns from here that roasting can also be called cooking.

sources.quote: לא מצאנו במקום אחר לשון "בשול" לצלי; לפיכך אמ' "באש" להודיע כי צלי היה
sources.says: Radak says the word for cooking is not used for roasting anywhere else, so the verse says "in fire" to show it was roasted.

sources.quote: למדנו מזה המקום שהצליה תקרא בשול ולזה אמרה התורה ובשל מבושל במים
sources.says: Ralbag says we learn from this verse that roasting is also called cooking, which is why the Torah had to say "boiled in water" when it forbade boiling.

35:20.headline: Pharaoh Necho's name means "the lame one"
35:20.body: Radak says נכו is a nickname, given because he was lame in the legs, like the phrase נכה רגלים. The Targum calls him "Pharaoh the lame".

sources.quote: "נכו" הוא שם כנוי, כמו שאומ' במלכים "פרעה נכה" (מ"ב כג,כט). ונקרא כן לפי שהיה נכה רגלים; וכן תרגם יונתן (שם): "פרעה חגירא"
sources.says: Radak says Necho is a nickname, given because he was lame in the legs, and that Targum Jonathan calls him "Pharaoh the lame".

sources.quote: נכו. ת״י חגירא והוא מענין שבירה וכן נכה רגלים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Targum renders it "lame", a word about breaking, as in "lame of feet".

sources.quote: סליק פרעה חגירא מלכא דמצרים
sources.says: The Targum says "Pharaoh the lame, king of Egypt, went up".

35:22.headline: Who was in disguise: Josiah, or Necho with a trick?
35:22.body: Most commentators say Josiah changed out of his royal clothes so he would not be recognized in battle. Malbim reads it the other way: Josiah thought Necho's talk of only passing through was a disguise for an attack.

sources.quote: ר"ל כי שנה בגדיו כדי שלא יכירוהו וילבש כלי מלחמה
sources.says: Ralbag says Josiah changed his clothes so he would not be recognized and put on armor.

sources.quote: התחפש. ענין לבישת בגדים משונים מבגדים שרגיל בהם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means putting on clothes different from the ones a person usually wears.

sources.quote: יאשיה חשב שהוא מתחפש להלחם בו, שמה שאומר שהולך דרך ארצו לכרכמיש הוא ערמה מאתו
sources.says: Malbim says Josiah thought Necho was the one in disguise, and that his claim to be heading to Carchemish was a trick.

35:25.headline: Princes and princesses, or men and women singers?
35:25.body: The Targum reads these words as nobles and noblewomen. Rashi and Metzudat David read them from שיר, song: the men and women who sang the laments for Josiah.

sources.quote: ויאמרו כל השרים. לשון שירה, משוררים; כי גם שירה וקינה בקול אחת נאמרין
sources.says: Rashi says השרים comes from the word for song, meaning singers, because song and lament are sung in the same voice.

sources.quote: השרים והשרות. המשוררים והמשוררות
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are the men and women singers.

sources.quote: ואמרין עמיה כל רברביא ומטרוניתא
sources.says: The Targum renders it "all the nobles and noblewomen said with him".

4:1.headline: A 'bronze altar' that was really made of stone
4:1.body: The verse says Solomon made a bronze altar. The Metzudat David and Malbim say it was a stone altar, made to replace the bronze altar Moses built in the desert.

sources.quote: מזבח נחושת. ר״ל מזבח אבן תחת מזבח נחשת שעשה משה במדבר
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it means a stone altar in place of the bronze altar Moses made in the desert.

sources.quote: היינו מזבח אבנים תחת מזבח נחשת של משה
sources.says: Malbim says it was an altar of stones in place of Moses' bronze altar.

4:2.headline: Ten across, thirty around: the sages' rule of three
4:2.body: The basin is ten cubits across, and a line of thirty cubits goes around it. Rashi, Radak and the Metzudat David explain with the Talmud's rule: anything three handbreadths around is one handbreadth across.

sources.quote: כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהֶקֵּיפוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, יֵשׁ בְּרָחְבּוֹ טֶפַח
sources.says: Rashi says anything three handbreadths around is one handbreadth wide.

sources.quote: שכל שיש בהקיפו שלשה טפחים יש בו רוחב טפח
sources.says: Radak gives the same rule: three handbreadths around means one handbreadth across.

sources.quote: כי כל מה שיש ברחבו אחד יש בהקיפו שלשה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says whatever is one across is three around.

4:3.headline: Oxen here, פקעים in Kings: ox faces on round shapes
4:3.body: Kings calls the decorations under the basin's rim פקעים; Chronicles calls them oxen. Radak and the Metzudat David say they are the same things: round, egg-like shapes made with the faces of oxen.

sources.quote: ובקרים שזכר הנה הם הפקעים שזכר בספר מלכים
sources.says: Radak says the oxen named here are the פקעים named in Kings.

sources.quote: נצטרך לפרש כי גופם היה עגול כדמות ביצים, ופניהם היו דמות פני בקרים
sources.says: Radak says, since the Aramaic renders פקעים as egg shapes, their bodies were round like eggs and their faces like oxen.

sources.quote: ובמ״א נאמר פקעים כי עשו בפקעים צורות ראשי בקרים
sources.says: The Metzudat David says Kings says פקעים because they made ox-head shapes on them.

4:9.headline: The Temple court is called עזרה, 'help'
4:9.body: The courtyard where the people stood is called the עזרה. Radak and the Metzudat David say it is named for help, עזר: people were helped by God when they prayed there.

sources.quote: היא החצר הגדולה שהיו עומדים בה ישראל
sources.says: Radak says it is the great court where Israel stood.

sources.quote: שהיו נעזרים בהתפללם שם
sources.says: Radak says it is called עזרה because people were helped when they prayed there.

sources.quote: וקרויה עזרה על כי נעזרים מה׳ כאשר יתפללו בה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it is called עזרה because people are helped by God when they pray in it.

4:10.headline: Why the basin stood off to the south side
4:10.body: Rashi says Solomon moved the basin away from the line of the entrance, toward the south of the court. It was not fitting for priests to immerse facing the doorway of the Temple hall.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין כָּבוֹד וְנָאֶה שֶׁיְּהוּ מַטְבִּילִין כְּנֶגֶד פֶּתַח הָאוּלָם
sources.says: Rashi says it was moved south because it is not honorable or fitting to immerse facing the entrance of the hall.

4:13.headline: 'The face' of the pillars means their top
4:13.body: The Metzudat Zion says על פני here means 'at the top'. Since a person's face is at the top of the body, the word for face is borrowed for height.

sources.quote: על פני. ר״ל בגבהם ועל כי פני האדם הוא בגובהו נקרא הגובה על פני בל׳ שאלה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it means at their height: since a person's face is at his top, height is called 'face' as a borrowed word.

4:16.headline: 'Huram his father': as skilled as his father, or with him?
4:16.body: Radak and the Metzudat David read חורם אביו as missing the letter כ, 'like his father': Huram worked as well as his famous father. Ralbag reads it as missing ו, 'Huram and his father': the two made the vessels together.

sources.quote: כל הכלים האלה עשה חירם יפים וטובים כאביו
sources.says: Radak says Hiram made all these vessels fine and good, like his father.

sources.quote: חורם אביו. הראוי כאביו ותחסר כ״ף השמוש
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it should read 'like his father', with the letter כ left out.

sources.quote: והרצון בו עשה חורם ואביו למלך שלמה
sources.says: Ralbag says it means Huram and his father made them for King Solomon.

4:17.headline: Zeredah: Jeroboam's town, and he 'narrowed' the Torah
4:17.body: Kings calls this place צרתן, and the Metzudat Zion says it went by both names. Rashi says Zeredah was Jeroboam's town, and cites his uncle's play on it: Jeroboam narrowed, הצר, the Torah of our God.

sources.quote: צרדתה. ובמ״א נאמר צרתן ובשתי השמות נקראה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says Kings calls it צרתן, and the place was called by both names.

sources.quote: צְרֵדָתָה הוּא מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל יָרָבְעָם
sources.says: Rashi says Zeredah is Jeroboam's place.

sources.quote: מִן צְרֵדָתָה – נִרְאֶה שֶׁהֵצַר הַתּוֹרָה וְלֹא הִרְחִיבָהּ; הֵצַר דַּת אֱלֹהֵינוּ
sources.says: Rashi reads 'from Zeredah' as showing that Jeroboam narrowed the Torah and did not widen it, narrowing the law of our God, as his uncle taught him.

4:21.headline: All gold, or gold refined a thousand times?
4:21.body: Radak reads מכלות as 'vessels': every part of the lampstand was gold. Others read it as 'perfect gold', refined again and again, and Radak cites the sages that each lampstand's gold went into the furnace a thousand times.

sources.quote: כל כלי המנורה הוא זהב
sources.says: Radak says it means all the lampstand's parts were gold.

sources.quote: זהב מזוקק הרבה
sources.says: Radak reports others who read it as gold refined many times.

sources.quote: והכניסוהו אלף פעמים לכור
sources.says: Radak cites the sages that they put it into the furnace a thousand times.

sources.quote: הוּא מִכְלוֹת זָהָב. מְזֻקָּק וְצָרוּף
sources.says: Rashi says מכלות זהב means refined, purified gold.

6:13.headline: Here ויברך means he knelt, not he blessed
6:13.body: ויברך usually means he blessed. Metzudat Zion says here it means he knelt, and "on his knees" was added to make that clear.

sources.quote: ויברך. ענין כריעה ולתוספת ביאור אמר על ברכיו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means kneeling, and the verse adds "on his knees" to explain.

6:19.headline: Not a song of joy but a cry for help
6:19.body: רנה often means a joyful song. Rashi says here it is a cry, as in "the cry went through the camp" in Kings.

sources.quote: זוֹ צְעָקָה, כְּמוֹ ״וַתַּעֲבֹר הָרִנָּה בַּמַּחֲנֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a cry, as in ותעבר הרנה במחנה, "the cry passed through the camp".

6:22.headline: Here נשא means owing, not lifting
6:22.body: נשא usually means to lift or carry. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as a debt: the law makes him owe an oath.

sources.quote: אם יחייבנו הדין שבועה, מענין "כי תשה ברעך משאת מאומה
sources.says: Radak says it means the law obliges him to swear, and the word is like the word for a loan in Deuteronomy.

sources.quote: ונשא. ענין חוב כמו כאשר נושא בו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a debt, as in כאשר נושא בו in Isaiah.

6:24.headline: Not "praise your name" but "confess"
6:24.body: והודו usually means they will give thanks. Rashi says here it means they will confess their sins.

sources.quote: פִּתְרוֹן: וְהִתְוַדּוּ אֶת עֲוֹנָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means they will confess their sin.

6:35.headline: Do their judgment: avenge them, or give them what they need?
6:35.body: Rashi gives two readings of משפטם: punish their enemies, or provide what they need.

sources.quote: נִקְמָתָם בְּאוֹיְבֵיהֶם. עִנְיָן אַחֵר: צָרְכֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means their revenge on their enemies, or else their needs.

sources.quote: לנקום נקמתם מיד העובדי כוכבים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means to avenge them on the idol worshippers.

6:41.headline: Why the Ark is called "Your strength"
6:41.body: Rashi says the Ark is called עזך, your strength, because of the wonders and mighty acts done through it among the Philistines.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם כֵּן קָרוּי עֻזֶּךָ, עַל שֶׁעָשָׂה נִפְלְאוֹתָיו וַעֲזוּזוֹת בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים
sources.says: Rashi says it is called עזך because of the wonders and mighty acts done among the Philistines.

6:41.headline: Your devoted ones: those who pray, or the Levite singers?
6:41.body: Radak gives two readings of חסידיך: the devout who sit in God's house to pray, or the Levites who sang in the Temple. Rashi takes them as the Levites, glad of the gifts they receive.

sources.quote: וכן חסידיך היושבים בביתך להתפלל ולדעת דרכיך
sources.says: Radak says they are the devout who sit in God's house to pray and learn His ways.

sources.quote: או פי' "וחסידיך": הלוים שהיו משוררים במקדש
sources.says: Radak says that, or else they are the Levites who sang in the Temple.

sources.quote: בְּרוֹב טוֹבוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת הַנִּתָּן לַלְוִיִּם בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁשּׁוֹמְרִין אֶת הָאָרוֹן וּמְשׁוֹרְרִים לְפָנָיו
sources.says: Rashi says they will rejoice in the gifts and tithes given to the Levites for guarding the Ark and singing before it.

9:11.headline: Harps not "for the princes" but "for the singers"
9:11.body: שרים usually means princes or officials. Metzudat David and Rashi read it from שיר, "song": the harps were for singers. Rashi gives two views: the Levite singers, or singers who entertained the king.

sources.quote: לשרים. למשוררים
sources.says: Metzudat David says לשרים means for the singers.

sources.quote: יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים לִבְנֵי לֵוִי הַמְשׁוֹרְרִים בִּכְלֵי שִׁיר
sources.says: Rashi says some explain it as the Levites who sang with instruments.

sources.quote: לַשָּׁרִים הַמְשׁוֹרְרִים לְטַיֵּל לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Eliezer: singers who sang to entertain the king.

9:15.headline: זהב שחוט: gold so soft it could be spun like thread
9:15.body: שחוט usually means slaughtered. Rashi hears חוט, "thread": gold so fine and soft it could be spun. Metzudat Zion reads it as drawn out, like "a drawn arrow" (Jeremiah 9:7), gold that stretches like wax.

sources.quote: זָהָב רַךְ וְנוֹחַ לְהֵרָקַע מֵרוֹב חֲשִׁיבוּתוֹ, שֶׁנִּטְוָה כְּחוּט
sources.says: Rashi says it is soft gold, easy to beat out, that was spun like thread.

sources.quote: נמשך כמו חץ שחוט (ירמיהו ט׳:ז׳) ור״ל זהב טוב הנמשך כשעוה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means drawn out, as in "a drawn arrow": good gold that stretches like wax.

9:18.headline: כבש: a golden ramp like the altar's, or a footrest
9:18.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read a smooth sloping ramp, not steps, like the ramp up to the Temple altar. Malbim reads it as the footrest under the king's feet.

sources.quote: אבל אינו עשוי כמעלות האבנים והעצים שהם זה על זה, אלא מעלה אחת לבד הוא, ומשופע הוא
sources.says: Radak says a כבש is not built of steps one above another, but is a single sloping incline.

sources.quote: לפיכך היו עושין למזבח כבש
sources.says: Radak says this is why the altar was built with a ramp.

sources.quote: עשוי כעין גשר משופע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is made like a sloping bridge.

sources.quote: וכבש בא על מדרך הרגל
sources.says: Malbim says כבש means the place where the feet rest.

9:21.headline: שנהבים: ivory tusks, or the elephants too
9:21.body: The word begins with שן, "tooth". Metzudat Zion and the Targum, cited by Radak, read elephant tusks. Rashi says the ships brought both ivory and the elephants themselves.

sources.quote: שנהבים. שן הפיל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שנהבים means elephant tusk.

sources.quote: תרגם יונתן בספר מלכים (מ"א י,כב): "שן דפיל וקופין וטוסין"
sources.says: Radak cites the Targum in Kings: "elephant tooth, apes and peacocks".

sources.quote: שֶׁנְהַבִּים. שֵׁן פִּיל וְפִיל עַצְמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means elephant tusk and the elephant itself.

9:25.headline: Not lions but horse stalls: 4,000 here, 40,000 in Kings
9:25.body: In verses 18 and 19 the same letters spell lions. Here Metzudat Zion reads stalls where horses feed. Kings counts 40,000, and Malbim settles it: 4,000 large stalls with ten rooms each.

sources.quote: אוריות. אבוסים כי אבוס בעליו (ישעיהו א׳:ג׳) תרגומו אוריא והוא מקום מאכל הבהמות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אוריות are feeding troughs: the Targum renders אבוס as אוריא, the place where animals eat.

sources.quote: ובמלכים: "ארבעים אלף ארות סוסים"
sources.says: Radak notes that Kings reads 40,000 stalls of horses.

sources.quote: בכל אוריה היו עשרה חדרים, נמצא היו ארבעה אלפים אוריות גדולות וארבעים אלף חדרים
sources.says: Malbim says each stall had ten rooms, so there were 4,000 large stalls and 40,000 rooms.
